assertion_results.text: Data extraction correctly identifies CVE-2026-31812, library quinn-proto, affected range < 0.11.14, and fixed version 0.11.14 from the Vulnerability issue (Step 1)
assertion_results.evidence: In data-extraction.md, the Step 1 table (lines 40-48) explicitly lists: CVE ID = CVE-2026-31812, Vulnerable library = quinn-proto, Affected version range = < 0.11.14, Fixed version = 0.11.14. All four data points are correctly extracted.

assertion_results.text: Data extraction identifies the ecosystem as Cargo based on the library name and component context (Step 1 Ecosystem detection)
assertion_results.evidence: In data-extraction.md, lines 63-71, the Ecosystem Detection section states: 'The vulnerable library is quinn-proto, a Rust crate. This maps to the Cargo ecosystem from the Ecosystem Mappings table in the 2.2.x stream's security-matrix.md.' It correctly identifies Lock File as Cargo.lock and Check Command as 'git show <tag>:Cargo.lock'.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table includes ALL versions from the security-matrix.md supportability matrix — no versions are skipped (Important Rule 4)
assertion_results.evidence: In version-impact.md, lines 14-21, the table includes 7 versions spanning both configured streams: 2.1.0, 2.1.1 (stream 2.1.x) and 2.2.0, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3, 2.2.4 (stream 2.2.x). Lines 5-8 confirm both streams' security-matrix.md files were loaded. The version numbering is contiguous within each stream with no gaps.

assertion_results.text: Version impact analysis uses pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix for each version, not branch HEAD (Important Rule 13)
assertion_results.evidence: In version-impact.md, lines 14-21, each version row has a specific pinned tag: 2.1.0=v0.3.8, 2.1.1=v0.3.12, 2.2.0=v0.4.5, 2.2.1=v0.4.8, 2.2.2=v0.4.9, 2.2.3=v0.4.11, 2.2.4=v0.4.12. These are individual commit tags, not branch HEAD references. The affects-versions.md further confirms tag-based lookup at lines 30-34, e.g., 'RHTPA 2.2.0 (tag v0.4.5) ships quinn-proto 0.11.9'.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table identifies retag versions and carries forward the affected status from the original version (Important Rule 5)
assertion_results.evidence: In version-impact.md, line 20: '2.2.2 | 2.2.x | v0.4.9 | -- | YES | retag of 2.2.1 (same as v0.4.8: 0.11.12)'. The quinn-proto column shows '--' (no independent lookup) and the notes explicitly identify it as a retag of 2.2.1, carrying forward the YES affected status from the original version 2.2.1.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction proposes replacing PSIRT-assigned versions with lock-file-verified versions, showing the diff (Step 3.2)
assertion_results.evidence: In affects-versions.md, lines 23-26 show the explicit diff: 'Current:  [RHTPA 2.0.0]' / 'Proposed: [RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2]'. Lines 28-34 provide rationale with lock-file-verified evidence for each version, referencing specific tags and quinn-proto versions found at those tags.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction references version names from the supportability matrix rather than hardcoded Jira version IDs (Important Rule 6)
assertion_results.evidence: In affects-versions.md, lines 14-18, proposed versions use names: RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2. The Jira mutation at lines 41-47 uses placeholder references like '<jira-id-for-RHTPA-2.2.0>' rather than hardcoded numeric IDs, and line 50 states: 'Jira version IDs would be discovered dynamically via getJiraIssueTypeMetaWithFields (Step 3.1). These are placeholder references -- the actual IDs are resolved at execution time.'

assertion_results.text: Remediation tasks include Repository, Target Branch, acceptance criteria, and dependency linkage between upstream and downstream tasks (Important Rule 9)
assertion_results.evidence: In remediation.md: Task 1 (upstream) has Repository: rhtpa-backend (line 40), Target Branch: release/0.4.z (line 44), Acceptance Criteria with 3 checkbox items (lines 72-74), and dependency linkage via jira.create_link with type 'Depend' to TC-8001 (lines 95-100). Task 2 (downstream) has Repository: rhtpa-release.0.4.z (line 121), Target Branch: main (line 125), Acceptance Criteria with 2 checkbox items (lines 147-148), and dependency linkage via Blocks link to upstream task (lines 175-182).

assertion_results.text: For Cargo ecosystem, remediation creates two tasks: upstream backport task and downstream propagation subtask with Blocks dependency (Important Rule 8)
assertion_results.evidence: In remediation.md: Task 1 is titled 'Upstream Backport Task (2.2.x)' (line 25) and Task 2 is titled 'Downstream Propagation Subtask (2.2.x)' (line 104). The Blocks dependency between them is established at lines 175-182: jira.create_link(inwardIssue: <upstream-task-key>, outwardIssue: <downstream-task-key>, type: 'Blocks'). Line 9 confirms this two-task structure is because 'quinn-proto is a Cargo (source dependency) ecosystem'.

assertion_results.text: The analysis presents triage recommendations as proposed actions — framing Affects Versions changes, label additions, and status transitions as proposals rather than executed mutations (Guardrails)
assertion_results.evidence: All mutation actions are consistently prefixed with 'PROPOSAL': affects-versions.md line 39 'PROPOSAL: Jira Mutation', line 54 'PROPOSAL: Correction Comment'; remediation.md line 27 'PROPOSAL: Create Jira Task' (Task 1), line 86 'PROPOSAL: Post description digest comment', line 93 'PROPOSAL: Link to Vulnerability issue', line 108 'PROPOSAL: Create Jira Task' (Task 2), line 371 'PROPOSAL: Add ai-cve-triaged label to TC-8001', line 377 'PROPOSAL: Post summary comment on TC-8001'. No actions are described as having been executed.

assertion_results.text: The data-extraction output describes Step 0.7 actions before the Step 1 data table: assigning the CVE issue to the current user and transitioning it to Assigned status (Step 0.7)
assertion_results.evidence: In data-extraction.md, lines 1-30 contain '# Step 0.7 -- Assign and Transition to Assigned' with four numbered actions: (1) retrieve current user's Jira account ID via jira.user_info(), (2) assign TC-8001 to current user via jira.edit_issue, (3) discover the Assigned transition dynamically via jira.get_transitions, (4) transition to Assigned status via jira.transition_issue. This entire section precedes '# Step 1 -- Data Extraction' which begins at line 35.
